principles: Prefer the smallest verified fix over broad refactors.
Do not weaken type checks, tests, security audit, or build gates to make a run green.
Do not add dependencies or expand gameplay scope as an incidental repair.
Keep fixes isolated and validate them before proposing them.
Unknown root causes require evidence and reproduction; do not guess.

cases.title: Phaser Scene property name collision
cases.rootCause: A custom scene field named lights collided with Phaser's inherited Scene.lights manager.
cases.resolution: Rename the game-specific collection to lightObjects and rerun typecheck, tests, and build.
cases.nextStep: Use a domain-specific property name rather than shadowing inherited Phaser Scene members.

cases.title: Vulnerable test-runner dependency tree
cases.rootCause: The original Vitest dependency tree included vulnerable versions in the test-runner dependency chain.
cases.resolution: Upgrade Vitest to the reviewed compatible version, then rerun npm audit, typecheck, unit tests, and production build.
cases.nextStep: Keep the explicit moderate-or-higher audit gate; do not suppress advisories just to pass CI.

cases.title: GitHub Pages cannot be enabled by workflow token
cases.rootCause: The workflow token lacks the repository-level permission required to enable Pages for this repository.
cases.resolution: A repository administrator must set Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source to GitHub Actions.
cases.nextStep: Do not keep retrying privileged enablement from CI. Enable Pages manually, then rerun deployment.

cases.title: npm dependency graph construction error
cases.rootCause: npm 10.9.9 repeatedly crashed while constructing its dependency graph in the GitHub runner, including after three install attempts and cache clears. This points to the npm installer/dependency-resolution path, not a demonstrated TypeScript or game-code defect; the underlying cause is not yet proven.
cases.resolution: The current mitigation upgrades CI to npm 11 before installing and keeps bounded retries. If the crash persists, generate and review a package-lock.json, then use npm ci for reproducible dependency resolution.
cases.nextStep: Verify the npm version and installation result in the next CI/Doctor run. Do not mark this incident resolved until a clean install and all quality gates pass.
